2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1.
3. Respondent No.2 who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.
4.

FIR in Crime No.109/2023 was registered by Holenarasipura Rural Police Station, Hassan District against unknown person initially for the offence punishable NC: 2024:KHC:37497 under Section 363 of IPC, on the basis of first information dated 28.09.2023 received from respondent No.2 herein who is the mother of the victim girl, aged about 17 years.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced.
The petitioner was arrested and produced before the jurisdictional Court on 18.12.2023 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
5. The bail application filed by the petitioner before the Sessions Court in Spl.C.No.47/2024 was dismissed on 06.06.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a youngster aged about 24 years having no criminal antecedents.
The petitioner and the victim girl are in love.

The victim girl has not made any allegation against the petitioner in her statement recorded before the NC:
2024:KHC:37497 jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C,.

Accordingly, he prays to Sri Mahesha L.M. @ Mahesh vs State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72106029/
2 allow the petition.

sentences.text:
7. Per contra, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 has opposed the petition.
8.

The material on record would go to show that FIR in Crime No.109/2023 was initially registered against unknown person for the offences punishable under Section 363 of IPC, on the basis of first information submitted by respondent No.2 herein.
In the first information it is stated that the victim girl aged about 17 years who was studying in I PUC who had gone to her college, had not returned home on 25.09.2023.
The efforts made to trace her by the first informant and her relatives had failed.
Therefore, the first informant had approached the police on 28.09.2023.
During the course of investigation, the victim girl and the petitioner were traced.
9. The statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, was recorded by the jurisdictional Magistrate on 26.12.2023.
In the said statement the NC: 2024:KHC:37497 victim girl has stated that her engagement was performed by her parents against her wishes.
She was in love with the petitioner, who is her mother's relative.
After her parents came to know about the same, they had stopped sending her to college.
This was informed by the victim girl to petitioner over phone.
Thereafter, the petitioner came near her house and together they traveled to Bengaluru and subsequently to Hassan where they stayed in the house of the petitioner's sister.
She has stated that on 18.12.2023 the petitioner had gone to Mysuru and the police arrested him and subsequently the victim girl was also brought back.
She has not made any allegation as against the petitioner about he committing sexual assault on her during the time she was with him from 25.09.2023 till the police traced her.
Even before the doctor, who had medically examined her she has stated that she was in love with the petitioner.
Undisputedly, the petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he is in custody from 18.12.2023.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

11. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.
